clue.text: Prohibition one put on speaker — it's silent all around

indicators.note: all around says the word for silent wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay silent

indicators.note: put on says the numeral for one is added after the word for a speaker

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A ban is slapped on a public speaker, with everyone around him keeping quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is only a link; the image of a hushed audience hides that 'silent' supplies the outer letters while 'all around' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A moratorium is a temporary ban or suspension of some activity.

clue.text: Finish up in heap? That's great folly

indicators.note: in says the turned word goes inside the word for heap

parts.note: a mass is a heap

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word for finish is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Ending up in a pile is a great piece of foolishness.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' signals reading a word from the bottom; 'in' then places it within the heap word.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness is extreme foolishness, lunacy.

clue.text: Academic has few callers — hero working

indicators.note: working says the letters of few callers and hero are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A scholar receives few visitors while a hero toils.
explanation.definitionFit: A research fellow is a university scholar employed to do research.

clue.text: So that has a triangular formation in maths?

definitions.text: that has a triangular formation in maths?
definitions.meaning: the maths symbol for consequently is three dots in a triangle

explanation.definitionFit: Therefore means consequently, and maths writes it as three dots arranged in a triangle.

clue.text: List organised to accommodate one member of club

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

indicators.note: to accommodate says the word for organised holds the numeral inside

parts.note: to run something is to organise it, so ran
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A roster is drawn up to find room for a single club member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' looks like an anagram signal, but here it is a past-tense synonym, ran; 'to accommodate' puts the numeral inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rotarian belongs to the Rotary Club, the international service society.

clue.text: Over the course of short day a French individual is ruined

indicators.note: over the course of says the other pieces span either side of the letter for day

parts.note: un is French for a
one is a single individual
D is the short form of day

explanation.surface: Within a brief day, a single Frenchman is brought to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the course of' sets UN and ONE either side of D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be undone is an old phrase for being ruined or destroyed.

clue.text: Composer contributing to festive season

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musician helps out over Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer.

clue.text: What, just before Christmas, offers many a window of opportunity?

definitions.text: What, just before Christmas, offers many a window of opportunity?

parts.words: What, just before Christmas, offers many a window of opportunity?
parts.note: a December card or box with little numbered flaps opened one per day, each window giving a chance of a treat

explanation.definitionFit: This countdown chart has a door to open each day of the run-up to Christmas, literal windows of opportunity.

clue.text: Islander about to get bronzed after cold start

indicators.note: after says the other pieces follow that letter
start means the opening letter of the word cold

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to tan is to be bronzed by the sun

explanation.surface: An island dweller gets a suntan after a chilly beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cretan is a native of the Greek island of Crete.

clue.text: Show contempt for hospital department making protest

parts.note: to diss someone is slang for showing them disrespect
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Someone disparages a hospital unit as a form of complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement voiced openly, a form of objection.

clue.text: Screen potential ruler?

definitions.meaning: a partition or screen splitting a room
one who divides could go on to rule, from the maxim divide and rule

explanation.definitionFit: A room partition separates spaces, and the saying 'divide and rule' makes whoever splits people up a would-be governor.

clue.text: Blank out in periods with little energy

parts.note: eras are periods of history
E is the abbreviation for energy, so a small version of the word

explanation.surface: Someone loses consciousness at intervals when tired.
explanation.definitionFit: To blank out writing is to wipe or delete it.

clue.text: Earn new bouquet coming back to life again

indicators.note: new says the letters of the word earn are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its scent

explanation.surface: Winning a fresh bunch of flowers revives someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like an adjective for the bouquet, but it signals rearranging the letters of 'Earn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means reborn or reviving, from the same root as renaissance.

clue.text: Religious group said to be in area separate from others?

parts.note: a sect is a religious faction
oral means spoken, said rather than written

explanation.surface: A cult is rumoured to live apart in its own district.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectoral describes things confined to one sector, a zone kept distinct from the rest.

clue.text: Small country building has prohibition outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for prohibition sits round the word for building

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
a hut is a simple building

explanation.surface: A little nation has a structure surrounded by an embargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhutan is a small Himalayan kingdom.

clue.text: Small island — it, over time, becomes a retreat

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the earlier pieces sit above the word for time

parts.note: Herm is one of the smaller Channel Islands
taken as written
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A tiny island, over the years, turns into a hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Herm is a small island near Guernsey in the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermitage is a secluded dwelling, a refuge from the world.

clue.text: Member of group as fantastic harmoniser? Not me

indicators.note: fantastic says the letters of harmoniser are wildly rearranged, with the letters of me removed

explanation.surface: A band member as a brilliant arranger of harmonies, but not this speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not me' removes M and E from HARMONISER before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: George Harrison was a member of the Beatles.

clue.text: Child's original present in box

indicators.note: original here means the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to present something is to offer it

explanation.surface: A youngster's first gift arrives packed in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox or chest for valuables.

clue.text: Repair part of the road surface

definitions.meaning: to mend shoes, or patch something roughly
a rounded stone used to pave a street

explanation.definitionFit: To cobble is to mend roughly, and a cobblestone is one stone of an old paved street.

clue.text: Sport at festival that can be justly criticised

parts.note: a fair is a festive gathering
a game is a sport

explanation.surface: Playing some match at a fete.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair game is an idiom for a person or thing open to legitimate attack or ridicule.

clue.text: Demanding fellow follows English team

indicators.note: follows says the word for fellow comes after the other pieces

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
a gent is a fellow

explanation.surface: A pushy man tags along behind an English side.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or requiring much effort, exacting.

clue.text: Admits having to have drink

parts.note: to own is to have
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to needing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess, admitting a fault.

clue.text: One shouting outside front of temple — building to encourage worshippers to come along?

definitions.text: building to encourage worshippers to come along?

indicators.note: outside says the shouter's word wraps round the letter taken from temple

parts.note: a bellower is someone who shouts loudly

indicators.note: front of means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A loud preacher bawls outside a temple to draw in the faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell tower houses church bells, rung to summon a congregation.

clue.text: River features repeatedly in battle

definitions.meaning: the letter T appears twice in the word battle

explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a river of north-east England, and the letter T, spelt out, appears twice in the word battle.

clue.text: Old tribe involved in vice nightly

indicators.note: involved in says the answer is a run of letters wrapped up inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Ancient people engaged in wickedness every night.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles the two words: v-ICE NI-ghtly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.

clue.text: Wild animal and duck getting into rows on sand and getting buried

indicators.note: on says the letter for sand follows the word for rows
getting into says the duck's letter enters the other pieces

parts.note: lines are rows
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O
S is an abbreviation for sand

explanation.surface: A big cat and a waterbird wander among rows on a beach and end up covered over.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a zero score in cricket, hence the round letter; 'on' and 'getting into' signal the joins, and 'getting buried' restates the duck's burial inside the rows.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is a female lion, a big cat of the wild.

clue.text: One without seat in bus travelling in East End

indicators.note: travelling says the letters of the words East End move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A passenger stands on a bus journeying through London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is a working-class district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: A standee is a passenger who must stand because no seat is free.

clue.text: Everyone knows it — so pretence is foolish?

indicators.note: foolish says the letters of so pretence are jumbled into a silly new arrangement

explanation.surface: A claim that pretending is daft, since the truth is common knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: An open secret is a supposed confidence that is in fact widely known.
